labels.label: lem:spread_top

hypotheses.paper: M first countable, connected, LPC, Hausdorff; S skeletal; M∖S slsc in M
hypotheses.note: hrel; plus hSc (M∖S semilocally simply connected as a space), the library's construction of the maximal covering, as in GX.spread_top

hypotheses.paper: sub-covering M̃^S → N → M; N Hausdorff, LPC, first countable
hypotheses.note: p, q branched coverings with q∘p = base (as in GX.spread_top); N T2/LPC/first countable are the standing hypotheses ruled by DEC-66(a)

hypotheses.paper: T thinner, first countable, LPC, Γ(N/M) T-continuous; R ⊆ ord_p(N) T-portly with agreement

hypotheses.note: ADDED hRc: p⁻¹(R) connected for the natural topology (the proof's 'R̂ weakly connected', l.2047), scoped to the two clauses that use it: (a)-connectedness and (e). (a) first countable/LPC, (b), the (c) equivalence and (d) hold without it. Implied by R portly for the natural topology (isPreconnected_preimage_of_isPortly), as in the paper's only application (l.2096). Necessary: GX.cex_spread_top_halfCut

(c) proved equivalent to GX.StrongLocallyConnectedOrd (the Claim's 'we may assume Ô ∩ R̂ connected', l.2029); (e) proved from (c) (with hRc). Necessary: GX.cex_spread_top_sector / GX.not_spreadTopConnCE refute (c) and (e) under every hypothesis, hRc included
(d) under N → M Galoisian (WP-27j's GX.spread_top_deck), which the proof's γ̄ (l.2071) needs

findings: l.1990–2004: lem:spread_top is false as printed. Counterexample (formal, GX.cex_spread_top_halfCut / GX.not_spreadTopPrinted): M = N = ℂ, S = ∅, q = id, p: M̃^∅ → ℂ the universal covering, R = {Im ≠ 0}, T = the topology of ℂ generated by the usual one and {Im ≥ 0}. All hypotheses hold; p⁻¹{Im ≥ 0} and p⁻¹{Im < 0} are p^*T-open, so p^*T is disconnected and (a), (e) fail. The proof uses 'N strongly connected' (l.2018) and 'R̂ weakly connected' (l.2047), neither of which is a hypothesis.

l.2047: 'R̂ is weakly connected' does not follow even when T is connected (informal, not formalized; the formal correction only needs the half-cut counterexample): M = N = ℂ*, S = ∅, p the universal covering (log), T cutting ℂ* along the positive real ray with the ray glued to the upper bank; p^*T splits M̃ into strips. Corrected form: assume p⁻¹(R) connected (true when R is portly for the natural topology, as in the application l.2096).

l.2029/2034: the Claim's 'We may assume that Ô ∩ R̂ is connected' is unproved (the argument lifts a path from x̂ to some point over z, not to ẑ) and is exactly (c): GX.isPortly_strongPullTop_iff_local. It fails (FORMAL, GX.cex_spread_top_sector, GX.not_spreadTopConnCE): M = N = ℂ, S = {0}, M̃^{0} ≅ 𝔻_∞ the logarithmic covering completed at 0 (GX.exists_homeomorph_maxBranched_qDisc), q = id, R = ℂ∖{0} (portly for both topologies, p⁻¹R connected), T = usual ⊓ generateFrom{{0} ∪ {Re > 0}} (first countable, LPC, agreeing with the usual topology on R). The preimage of the sector is p^*T-open and p^*T-connected through the branch point, its regular part p⁻¹{Re > 0} is not connected: (c), (e) and the Claim's local hypothesis all fail. theo:local_virt_tame uses (c)/(e) through (D) and the strong branched covering; its proof inherits the gap.

l.2025: 'M̃^S → M is Galoisian and thus so is M̃^S → N' is asserted without argument; it is true (GX.isGaloisian_of_comp: deck transitivity over q⁻¹(M∖S) by uniqueness of lifts, dense orbits, discrete fibres from M∖S slsc in M), using N Hausdorff, LPC, first countable and M∖S ⊆ ord_q (GX.compl_subset_ordY_of_comp).

l.2017–2018 'lem:path_covering' is applied relative to an open connected O (GX.exists_path_of_isPortly_of_isOpen), and the Claim's second part needs fibres of p discrete (from M∖S slsc in M) to pick Ô ∩ p⁻¹(y) = {ŷ}.
questions: Strongest true form: (c) and (e) hold exactly under the local hypothesis GX.StrongLocallyConnectedOrd (which may be what 'we may assume' intends as a hypothesis on T); rule whether theo:local_virt_tame should carry it, and whether the corrected form with hRc and StrongLocallyConnectedOrd closes the row.

labels.label: rem:intuitively_spread_thinner_than

hypotheses.paper: p a spread, T thinner than T_N
hypotheses.note: the coarsest-bound half needs neither: every locally connected σ' finer than T_M with p σ'→T continuous is finer than p^*T

findings: l.2006: read literally, 'p^*T is the coarsest topology on M such that (M,p^*T) → (N,T) is a spread' is false — p^*T need not be a spread at all (GX.not_isSpread_strongPullTop_ratTop: p = id on ℝ, T generated by the usual topology and ℚ; p^*T is not locally connected at √2). The true content: every spread topology finer than T_M is finer than p^*T, and p^*T is the coarsest one exactly when it is locally connected (GX.isSpread_strongPullTop_iff, GX.isGreatest_strongPullTop). The remark's own 'However' sentence is GX.cex_component_not_strongPull_connected (ℝ cut at 0). The proof block following the remark (l.2010–2061) is the proof of lem:spread_top, formalized under that label.
questions: Reading of 'intuitively': the formal statements above (coarsest among spread topologies whenever p^*T is one; iff locally connected; with the two examples). Rule whether the row closes under this reading.

labels.label: rem:hypothesis_model_spaces_necessary

hypotheses.paper: θ ∉ {0, 2π}, E_θ^{1,2} as a singular model, T the BTZ tamifying topology
hypotheses.note: abstract: any T finer than the natural topology and any open V; non-vacuous by the toy instance GX.hypothesis_model_spaces_toy (ℝ, cutTopReal, V = (-1,∞), translation by 2); the model E_θ^{1,2} with the BTZ tamifying topology is not built

findings: l.2148: 'V ⊂ {t>0} or V ⊂ {t>0}' — the second should read {t<0}.

l.2141–2145: the assertion that the mixed topology T' (natural ⊔ T|{t>0}) is again tamifying (first countable, LPC, (A)–(D)) is asserted without argument; local path-connectedness at points of ∂{t>0} where T is strictly finer is not obvious (a natural-topology path entering {t>0} through such a point must be T-continuous there).
questions: Not built, forward dependency: the massive particle E_θ^{1,2}, its maximal covering, and the BTZ tamifying topology T on it — §4's prop:BTZ_virt_tame (l.2252) — and the isomorphism of BTZ̃ → BTZ with Ẽ_θ → E_θ in the category of spreads; the remark's concrete claims rest on them. Formalized: the mechanism (Γ-invariance without Aut-invariance) for an abstract T and V, with a toy instance.

labels.label: rem:quotient_virtually_tame

hypotheses.paper: N → M some branched covering possibly branched above sing(M); N with the quotient of a tamifying topology T
hypotheses.note: read through the universal property: Pj : M̃ → N onto with π_N ∘ Pj = base, N with coinduced Pj T; for Γ_N ⊆ Γ(N/M) (descend_mem_deckMapsOf) Pj continuous and open for the natural topologies (any branched covering)

ADDED: M̃ → M Galoisian. Used: it makes the fibres of N → M the orbits of the descended Γ(M̃/M). Holds when reg M is semi-locally simply connected in M (maxBranched_isGaloisian_cc). Not shown necessary (no counterexample known): a narrowing, not a refutation

hypotheses.paper: D injective developing map; Γ acts via the holonomy
hypotheses.note: D continuous for the quotient of T, injective, D ∘ Pj equivariant under Γ(M̃/M) through ρ (data); injectivity makes every γ descend to N (exists_descend_of_injective), so N → M is Galoisian
proved as topological spaces: D(N) → M is a continuous open surjection (quotient map) with the ρ(Γ_N)-orbits as fibres, Γ_N ⊆ Γ(N/M) the descents; not as singular (G,X)-manifolds

findings: l.2154: the remark's identification uses that the fibres of N → M are Γ(N/M)-orbits; this follows (descend_mem_deckMapsOf, quotient_virtually_tame_cover) from injectivity of D when M̃ → M is Galoisian, which the remark does not state. The previous round's claim that the remark is false for non-Galoisian N is WITHDRAWN (no counterexample; for an injective developing map every γ ∈ Γ(M̃/M) descends). Recorded as a narrowing.
questions: Is 'M̃ → M Galoisian' meant to be part of 'virtually tamely singular' (e.g. via locally Galoisian), or should the remark carry it? And does 'isomorphic' mean as singular (G,X)-manifolds (needs prop:aeGXquotient's structure on Γ\D(N))?

kb_proposals: A second topology T on a type that already has an instance is a LOCAL INSTANCE: declare it BEFORE the ambient instance in `variable`/binders ({T : TopologicalSpace N} [tN : TopologicalSpace N]) so that unannotated lemmas resolve to tN, and call every lemma that should use T with @ (IsOpen.inter, Path.source, Homeomorph.symm, IsBranchedCovering projections). A binder T : TopologicalSpace (MaxBranchedCover …) overrides even the GLOBAL SpreadEnd instance — put hypotheses about the weak topology before T.
unitInterval has no LocallyConnectedSpace instance at this pin: `(convex_Icc (0:ℝ) 1).locPathConnectedSpace` (GX.locPathConnectedSpace_unitInterval_sptop).
Continuity into p^*T from a locally connected source = continuity for the source topology + T-continuity of p ∘ f (GX.continuous_strongPullTop_iff): the workhorse for two-topology path arguments.
complete_path_carac has a universe parameter in HomotopyLiftExtends: call it as @complete_path_carac.{0} … when its instances are passed by @.

The maximal covering of ℂ branched over {0} is 𝔻_∞ over ℂ (GX.exists_homeomorph_maxBranched_qDisc): logChart makes q⁻¹(ℂ∖0) ≅ ℂ contractible, UniversalCover.exists_homeomorph_of_simplyConnected + IsFoxCompletion.existsUnique_extend + maxBranched_unique. Use it to compute anything about \widetilde ℂ^{0} concretely.
